papers.version_note: arXiv:2411.00953v1 [physics.optics], 1 Nov 2024, compiled November 5, 2024. The text layer holds the paper once; the reference list appears twice (short and full).
papers.what_it_is: An optics letter that demonstrates, by experiment, a classifier of one versus two close-by incoherent light sources that uses optimized pump-shaped projection modes in sum frequency generation and keeps its fidelity under centroid misalignment and unequal source brightness.
papers.why_not: The paper is quantum-inspired optical super-resolution (spatial mode demultiplexing by nonlinear optics). It has no quantum computing workload and no machine learning model; the only optimization is classical particle swarm optimization of pump-mode coefficients. It fits none of qml, qc, ml, world or method; the context label on each assertion is the nearest fit (qc) and is not a claim that the paper bears on quantum computing.

assertions.value: The authors report a classification fidelity of over 80% even when the centroid is misaligned by half the source separation, or when one source is four times stronger than the other.
